results.title: 第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図（農研機構）Rapid Survey Map in Kanto Plain (1880 (Meiji 13)-1886 (Meiji 19), 1:20000)- コピー
results.description:
国立研究開発法人農業・食品産業技術総合研究機構（農研機構）が配信している第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図です。
：農研機構 WMS レイヤ（https://www.finds.jp/mapprv/wms.html.ja#LAYER）

第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図（ダイイチグンカンクチホウニマンブンノイチジンソクソクズゲンズ）は、参謀本部陸軍部測量局が 1880（明治13）年～ 1886（明治19）年に測量を実施し、随時発行された原図群で、範囲は関東平野、房総半島の大半が含まれています。

全図に彩色が施されており、詳細な土地利用分類が記載されていることが特徴です。例えば、林地を表す判例には、松、 杉，楢，椚などの樹種分類があり、当時の里山景観を知る手がかりを提供しています。また、軍事的な用途で作製された経緯から、 陣地構築に活用できる、または行軍の妨げになる、崖や土手などの情報は、特に詳細に描かれています。現在では姿をとどめない江戸時代の城下町（忍城、川越城など）や、戦国時代の城郭の縄張り（滝山城、皆川城など）を確認できる場合もあり、当時の関東地方の様子を伝える貴重な資料といえます。各図は、縮尺 1/20,000 でおおよそ統一されており、全 921 面が作製されました。

本図に関する詳しい情報は、歴史地理学紀要第21巻、地図と歴史地理「二万分一迅速測図の内容について（http://hist-geo.jp/pdf/archive/kiyou/021_103.pdf）」（出版：歴史地理学会、著者：清水靖夫氏）等をご参照ください。

農研機構では、地図画像配信サービスの公開に先立って"明治初期の土地利用は里地里山の原景観ともいえ、現在の土地利用と比較することで身近な生物多様性の保全や農業環境の管理に活用できます。" と公開の意義を強調しており、様々な分野での活用が期待されています。農研機構の歴史的農業環境閲覧システムは、第1回電子国土賞・コンテンツ部門を受賞しています。
：明治初期の土地利用は里地里山の原景観（http://www.naro.affrc.go.jp/archive/niaes/techdoc/press/080416/press080416.html）





・埼玉県所沢市三芳町周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
江戸時代の新田開発で整備された三富新田です。各家族は、道路に直行する短冊状の土地を所有し、道路に近い土地から屋敷地→畑地→林地を整備した畑作新田村の代表例です。ベースマップと見比べると、この当時の地割が現在にも引き継がれていることがわかります。


・渋谷駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
現在の渋谷駅周辺は、等高線が接近した谷地であることがわかります。谷底では、水田が営まれていました。
国木田独歩はこのあたりの高台に居を構え、急速に都市化の進む周囲の風景や、後背に広がる武蔵野台地の田園風景を見ながら、随筆「武蔵野」を執筆しました。


・赤羽駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
中心を横切る荒川河道の北方に堤防が築かれています。ベースマップと見比べると、現在の河道は変化してますが、当時の河道跡が現在の埼玉県川口市、東京都北区の行政境界として今も利用されていることがわかります。

：明治初期の土地利用は里地里山の原景観（https://www.naro.affrc.go.jp/archive/niaes/techdoc/press/080416/press080416.html）





・埼玉県所沢市三芳町周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
江戸時代の新田開発で整備された三富新田です。各家族は、道路に直行する短冊状の土地を所有し、道路に近い土地から屋敷地→畑地→林地を整備した畑作新田村の代表例です。ベースマップと見比べると、この当時の地割が現在にも引き継がれていることがわかります。


・渋谷駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
現在の渋谷駅周辺は、等高線が接近した谷地であることがわかります。谷底では、水田が営まれていました。
国木田独歩はこのあたりの高台に居を構え、急速に都市化の進む周囲の景観や、後背に広がる武蔵野台地の田園を見ながら、随筆「武蔵野」を執筆しました。


・赤羽駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
中心を横切る荒川河道の北方に堤防が築かれています。ベースマップと見比べると、現在の河道は変化してますが、当時の河道跡が現在の埼玉県川口市、東京都北区の行政境界として今も利用されていることがわかります。

results.description:
「ArcGIS Pro 学習用テキスト」のうち、「操作演習テキストA」としてまとめたものです。
操作演習テキストは、ArcGIS Pro のHelp にある「ArcGIS Pro クイックスタート チュートリアル」をもとに、一部を厳選して抜粋し、約6時間で演習が終了できるように再編したものになります。また、演習データはテキスト内に入手先が記載されていますが、一部の演習では、日本国内のデータに差し替えしているものもあります。

results.description:
「ArcGIS Pro 学習用テキスト」は、はじめてArcGIS Pro を触る方から、もっとArcGIS Pro を習熟したい方など、さまざまな方々にご利用いただけるように、「GIS の基礎知識と知って得する各種リソース」、「操作演習テキストA」、「操作演習テキストB」としてとりまとめたもので、このページからは、3つをまとめてダウンロード可能です。
操作演習テキストとしては、A とB の2 種類がありますが、B のテキストを利用する場合、予めA の操作の習得、もしくは相当するArcGIS Pro クイックスタートチュートリアルの操作を習得していることを推奨します。
操作演習テキストA と B は、ArcGIS Pro のHelp にある「ArcGIS Pro クイックスタート チュートリアル」をもとに、一部を厳選して抜粋し、それぞれ約6時間で演習が終了できるように再編したものになります。また、演習データはテキスト内に入手先が記載されていますが、一部の演習では、日本国内のデータに差し替えしているものもあります。

results.title: 第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図（農研機構）Rapid Survey Map in Kanto Plain (1880 (Meiji 13)-1886 (Meiji 19), 1:20000)- コピー
results.description:
国立研究開発法人農業・食品産業技術総合研究機構（農研機構）が配信している第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図です。
：農研機構 WMS レイヤ（https://www.finds.jp/mapprv/wms.html.ja#LAYER）

第一軍管区地方2万分1迅速測図原図（ダイイチグンカンクチホウニマンブンノイチジンソクソクズゲンズ）は、参謀本部陸軍部測量局が 1880（明治13）年～ 1886（明治19）年に測量を実施し、随時発行された原図群で、範囲は関東平野、房総半島の大半が含まれています。

全図に彩色が施されており、詳細な土地利用分類が記載されていることが特徴です。例えば、林地を表す判例には、松、 杉，楢，椚などの樹種分類があり、当時の里山景観を知る手がかりを提供しています。また、軍事的な用途で作製された経緯から、 陣地構築に活用できる、または行軍の妨げになる、崖や土手などの情報は、特に詳細に描かれています。現在では姿をとどめない江戸時代の城下町（忍城、川越城など）や、戦国時代の城郭の縄張り（滝山城、皆川城など）を確認できる場合もあり、当時の関東地方の様子を伝える貴重な資料といえます。各図は、縮尺 1/20,000 でおおよそ統一されており、全 921 面が作製されました。

本図に関する詳しい情報は、歴史地理学紀要第21巻、地図と歴史地理「二万分一迅速測図の内容について（http://hist-geo.jp/pdf/archive/kiyou/021_103.pdf）」（出版：歴史地理学会、著者：清水靖夫氏）等をご参照ください。

農研機構では、地図画像配信サービスの公開に先立って"明治初期の土地利用は里地里山の原景観ともいえ、現在の土地利用と比較することで身近な生物多様性の保全や農業環境の管理に活用できます。" と公開の意義を強調しており、様々な分野での活用が期待されています。農研機構の歴史的農業環境閲覧システムは、第1回電子国土賞・コンテンツ部門を受賞しています。
：明治初期の土地利用は里地里山の原景観（http://www.naro.affrc.go.jp/archive/niaes/techdoc/press/080416/press080416.html）





・埼玉県所沢市三芳町周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
江戸時代の新田開発で整備された三富新田です。各家族は、道路に直行する短冊状の土地を所有し、道路に近い土地から屋敷地→畑地→林地を整備した畑作新田村の代表例です。ベースマップと見比べると、この当時の地割が現在にも引き継がれていることがわかります。


・渋谷駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
現在の渋谷駅周辺は、等高線が接近した谷地であることがわかります。谷底では、水田が営まれていました。
国木田独歩はこのあたりの高台に居を構え、急速に都市化の進む周囲の風景や、後背に広がる武蔵野台地の田園風景を見ながら、随筆「武蔵野」を執筆しました。


・赤羽駅周辺の様子（マップでジャンプ）
中心を横切る荒川河道の北方に堤防が築かれています。ベースマップと見比べると、現在の河道は変化してますが、当時の河道跡が現在の埼玉県川口市、東京都北区の行政境界として今も利用されていることがわかります。

results.title: All about Shibuya (渋谷)
results.description:
“Instagrammable” refers to posts that can be visually and aesthetically pleasing or worthy enough to share on a platform that revolves around posting images called Instagram. Pictures taken on a high angle or on top of buildings are considered ‘Instagrammable’ for panoramic views, unique angles, city skylines, sunsets and golden hour, sense of adventure, framing opportunities, and exclusivity. People in social media love seeing posts with extravagance, or something they dream about achieving or traveling to one day.

Pictures that are taken from high angles of known skyscrapers such as Shibuya Sky are always considered ‘Instagrammable’ because it checks lots of boxes in the factors stated above. It’s not something people would be able to go or see daily, and that’s why people love to view these kinds of rooftop photos. Panoramic views, skylines, sunsets will always leave people in awe because it’s very visually and aesthetically pleasing to one’s eye.

results.title: Foothill Yellow-Legged Frog (North Coast DPS) Range - CWHR A043a [ds3344]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. Each focal taxon’s location data was extracted (when applicable) from the following list of sources. BIOS datasets are bracketed with their “ds” numbers and can be located on CDFW’s BIOS viewer: https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS.

  • California Natural Diversity Database,

  • Terrestrial Species Monitoring [ds2826],

  • North American Bat Monitoring Data Portal,

  • VertNet,

  • Breeding Bird Survey,

  • Wildlife Insights,

  • eBird,

  • iNaturalist,

  • other available CDFW or partner data.
tags: California Department of Fish And Wildlife
results.snippet:
The species range dataset represents the generalized geographic area within which the species is expected to regularly occur within California, without consideration of specific habitat requirements. Generally, range map boundaries are based on mapped species occurrence locations and expert knowledge and aligned with ecologically relevant units such as ecoregions or watersheds. The California Wildlife Habitat Relationship (CWHR) ranges have been developed over three decades and vary in age of last update. The date of last update can be found in the CWHR Revision Tracking Table at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=115517. 

GIS vector datasets representing species ranges are one component of the CWHR system. This system includes a web application that supplies information on California’s terrestrial vertebrates and the habitats upon which they depend, supports user queries, and houses spatial data on habitats and wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species that occur in California. CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of regularly occurring terrestrial vertebrate species within California. These range datasets are used to generate a tabular database of species locations by county, ecoregion, and several other jurisdictional delineations to inform the CWHR system. This enables users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. The species range datasets are also used by many groups to assist with development of biological surveys, and within CDFW to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning. 

For more information about the CWHR system, visit the CWHR Homepage: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

Appropriate uses of CWHR data include planning for site-specific biological surveys or anticipating general trends in habitat suitability for particular species resulting from management actions which may reshape habitat composition and structure (see comparison queries in the CWHR application). Neither the CWHR GIS data representing a species’ range, nor the data representing predicted suitable habitat replace the need for field surveys to confirm the presence or potential absence of a particular species at any specific site. Similarly, GIS data concerning the distribution of habitats does not replace the need for field surveys to verify the composition of habitat or vegetation communities at any specific site.

results.title: Recycling Collection Zone A
results.description:
What the data represents:
This dataset defines the geographic service area for residential recycling collections within Collection Zone A of the City of Albany waste management service area.
The layer contains polygon boundaries used to identify properties assigned to Recycling Zone A and supports property-based waste service enquiries through the Residential Waste Collection and Facilities application.
Recycling collections occur on a fortnightly schedule. Collection weeks alternate with Recycling Collection Zone B to support scheduled recycling services across the municipality.
The dataset may also contain service information including collection day, collection provider, contact details, and related service administration information.


Intended use:
Waste service administration, customer service enquiries, property-based waste searches, public information applications, and waste collection planning.


Data limitations:

  • Collection schedules may change due to public holidays, service interruptions, operational requirements, or future service reviews.
  • Service boundaries may be amended as new developments occur.
  • The dataset is intended to identify collection areas and should not be relied upon as a legal property service entitlement record.
  • Users should confirm service details through official City of Albany customer service channels where required.
  • Collection schedules displayed within public applications should be considered current at the time of publication only.
     

Data Owner: City of Albany – Sustainability and Waste
Source of Truth: City of Albany ArcGIS Online
Update Method/Frequency: Updated as waste service boundaries, collection schedules, or contractor arrangements are revised.
Data Export Requests: Self-service.
Public Display (AGOL): No restrictions.

results.title: AEDs
results.description:
What is AED?

Portable electronic devices that automatically diagnose potentially life threatening cardiac arrhythmias, commonly known as automated external defibrillators or AEDs.

How was this layer created?
This layer was created from deploying AED Locator solution, ArcGIS Solution for local government from here.  The raw data was downloaded from here. After cleaning attribute column and with the help of Open Street Map geocoding service, approximately 55% of records were geocoded with their available attributes (SITEID, NAME, MUNICIPALITY).  


Why was this layer created?

This layer was created for following three reasons:
1) To create an inventory of all the AEDs in British Columbia in Canada to assist emergency services to quickly locate the closest AED from the incident that involves cardiac arrest.
2) To showcase the result of the  BC - Public Access to Defibrillators program 
3) To illustrate the use of ArcGIS online platform to quickly deploy geo apps from ArcGIS Solutions for Local Government

results.title: 15.a.1a. Biologinės įvairovės apsaugai, kraštovaizdžio tvarkymui ir išsaugojimui skirtos lėšos (LT)
results.description:
LT
15 TIKSLAS. Saugoti, atkurti ir skatinti darnų sausumos ekosistemų naudojimą, darniai valdyti miškus, kovoti su dykumėjimu, sustabdyti žemės būklės blogėjimą ir pakeisti šį procesą priešinga kryptimi bei sustabdyti biologinės įvairovės praradimą:
Siekiama apsaugoti, atkurti ir skatinti sausumos, vidaus vandenų, miškų, pelkių, sausumų ekosistemų išsaugojimą ir tausų naudojimą. Tai apima pastangas ir finansinius išteklius siekiant tvariai valdyti miškus ir sustabdyti jų naikinimą, kovoti su dykumėjimu, atkurti sunykusią žemę ir dirvožemį, sustabdyti biologinės įvairovės nykimą ir apsaugoti nykstančias rūšis.
15.a. Uždavinys: Sutelkti ir labai padidinti finansinius išteklius iš visų šaltinių, siekiant išsaugoti ir tausiai naudoti biologinę įvairovę ir ekosistemas.
15.a.1. JT rodiklis: (a) Oficiali parama vystymuisi, skirta biologinės įvairovės išsaugojimui ir tvariam naudojimui; (b) gautos pajamos ir mobilizuotas finansavimas iš ekonominių priemonių, susijusių su biologine įvairove.
     Matavimo vienetai: Mln. EUR
Šaltinis: Lietuvos Respublikos aplinkos ministerija

EN
Goal 15. Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss:
The aim is to protect, restore and promote conservation and sustainable use of terrestrial, inland waters, forests, wetlands and terrestrial ecosystems. This covers efforts and financial resources to sustainably manage forests and halt deforestation, combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, halt biodiversity loss and protect endangered species.
15.a. Goal: Mobilize and significantly increase financial resources from all sources to conserve and sustainably use biodiversity and ecosystems.
15.a.1. UN indicator: (a) Official development assistance on conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; and (b) revenue generated and finance mobilized from biodiversity-relevant economic instruments.
     Units: Million EUR
Source: Ministry of Environment

results.title: LAP2017_dCDP2021_Flood_Zone_A
results.description:
Publication Date:

21st August, 2017

Abstract:

This dataset contains a set of Polygons identifying the areas at risk of flooding (Flood Zone A) which are included in the MD LAP and Draft CDP 2021 settlements.

Purpose:

As part of the preparation of the 2017 Local Area Plan the Council  updated the flood zone mapping used in the 2011 Local Area Plans to take account of the information that  became available from the National CFRAM programme (Catchment Flood Risk Assessment and Management), and other Flood Schemes undertaken by the OPW.  In addition, flood risk mapping for rural areas, outside of settlements boundaries, was available and was  published simultaneously with the Local Area Plan. This Mapping layer has been carried forward in the Draft Cork County Development Plan 2021.

The current CDP 2014 sets out the Council’s policy in relation to Flood Risks, in WS 6-1 Flood Risks – Overall Approach which states that in areas where there is a high probability of flooding – ‘Zone A’ – it is an objective to this plan to avoid development other than ‘water compatible development’ as described in Section 3 of the ‘Planning System and Flood Risk Management – Guidelines for Planning Authorities’ issued by the DoEHLG in November 2009.

Please refer to both these guidelines and the CDP 2014 (Chapter 11) for further information.

The policy proposed in the Draft Cork County development Plan 2021 is set out in Chapter 11 Water management and carries over the policy as set out in the 2014 CDP.

Status:

Final-As published in the Local Area Plans 2017/Draft Cork County Development Plan 2021

results.name: biosds3347_fpu
results.title: Foothill Yellow-Legged Frog (Central Coast DPS) Range - CWHR A043d [ds3347]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. Each focal taxon’s location data was extracted (when applicable) from the following list of sources. BIOS datasets are bracketed with their “ds” numbers and can be located on CDFW’s BIOS viewer: https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS.

  • California Natural Diversity Database,

  • Terrestrial Species Monitoring [ds2826],

  • North American Bat Monitoring Data Portal,

  • VertNet,

  • Breeding Bird Survey,

  • Wildlife Insights,

  • eBird,

  • iNaturalist,

  • other available CDFW or partner data.

results.snippet:
The species range dataset represents the generalized geographic area within which the species is expected to regularly occur within California, without consideration of specific habitat requirements. Generally, range map boundaries are based on mapped species occurrence locations and expert knowledge and aligned with ecologically relevant units such as ecoregions or watersheds. The California Wildlife Habitat Relationship (CWHR) ranges have been developed over three decades and vary in age of last update. The date of last update can be found in the CWHR Revision Tracking Table at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=115517. 

GIS vector datasets representing species ranges are one component of the CWHR system. This system includes a web application that supplies information on California’s terrestrial vertebrates and the habitats upon which they depend, supports user queries, and houses spatial data on habitats and wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species that occur in California. CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of regularly occurring terrestrial vertebrate species within California. These range datasets are used to generate a tabular database of species locations by county, ecoregion, and several other jurisdictional delineations to inform the CWHR system. This enables users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. The species range datasets are also used by many groups to assist with development of biological surveys, and within CDFW to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning. 

For more information about the CWHR system, visit the CWHR Homepage: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

results.licenseInfo:
This CWHR dataset should not be used to extend any analytical inference beyond that warranted by the nature of the data as it has been described in all sections of this metadata. Appropriate uses of CWHR data include planning for site-specific biological surveys or anticipating general trends in habitat suitability for particular species resulting from management actions which may reshape habitat composition and structure (see comparison queries in the CWHR application). Neither the CWHR GIS data representing a species’ range, nor the data representing predicted suitable habitat replace the need for field surveys to confirm the presence or potential absence of a particular species at any specific site. Similarly, GIS data concerning the distribution of habitats does not replace the need for field surveys to verify the composition of habitat or vegetation communities at any specific site.

results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. results.name: 248a_Sites_and_Dockets_Reference
results.title: VT Data - 248a Permitted Sites
results.description:
This dataset represents the locations permitted by the 30 V.S.A § 248a application process to host telecommunications equipment in the State of Vermont. Basic information about each host site is available from this data set and a related table includes basic information that references the associated dockets, which are the approved application material associated with each site, or any modification that takes place there.

Site locations are based on E911 Site Location (address points). Locations are referred to by their E911 Primary Address and E911 Location ID and include categorical information referred to as Site Types. These categories offer generic descriptors of the structure associated with the location.

Please note, there may be discrepancies between the petition or order location information from the docket and the E911 location. Oftentimes, applications are submitted prior to an E911 address being issued for a site. Inclusion in this dataset only indicates the issuance of a permit; no study has been completed to determine if towers have been constructed or to verify the listed data drawn from the permit applications.

This data is continually updated. PSD-Telecom generally waits to include a new location only after an E911 address has been assigned.


Field Descriptions

Sites_248a

ESITEID - This unique numeric ID is assigned to each point in the E911 Site Location dataset.

PRIMARYADD - This is the E911 Site Location field Primary Address. 

SITETYPE - This category is assigned by E911 and describes the general use of the structure assigned the ID and address.

TOWNNAME -This is the town. From E911 Site Location.

SITETYPE_M - Extra field for more additional site type classification.

SITETYPE_1 - Extra field for more additional site type classification.

SITETYPE_2 - Extra field for more additional site type classification.

SITETYPE_3 - Extra field for more additional site type classification.

SITETYPE_4 - Extra field for more additional site type classification.

COUNTY -This is the county. From E911 Site Location.

Structure Type - General description of building that houses the permitted telecommunications equipment.

Structure – Above Ground Level - (AGL) Total height in feet of structure that hosts the permitted telecommunications equipment.


Docket_248a_Relates

ESITE - This unique numeric ID is assigned to each point in the E911 Site Location dataset.

Case Number - This unique alphanumeric ID uses two formats. A legacy format was used prior to 2017 and is four numbers and were in sequence. The current format – YY-IDID-PET – includes two-digit year YY, a four-digit sequential ID number, and the designation PET for petition.

ePUC URL - This links directly to the records associated with the associated case number on the ePUC website.

Petitioner - Identifies the party making the application, per the docket information.

Date - For legacy dockets, this field indicates the date a decision was issued. For current dockets, this field indicates the date the application was made.

Petition Type - Lists programmatic category of the petition: “de minimus modification” of existing structure, projects of “limited size and scope,” or Regular.

Application – Structure Type - describes nature of tower construction, or generic description of host structure.

Case Name - This is the full name of the application case from the docket.

Application Structure Height - This is the height at which the equipment was permitted for.

Application – Address - This is the address of the location for the equipment, per the application.

Application – City - This is the municipality in which the structure that hosts the communication equipment is located.
results.snippet: A public reference of permitted 248a telecommunications equipment locations and a quick reference to the related docket information.

results.name: Adults_with_a_Disability
results.title: Adults with a Disability
results.description:
Estimates are for noninstitutionalized civilian population.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, disability describes “any condition of the body or mind (impairment) that makes it more difficult for the person with the condition to do certain activities (activity limitation) and interact with the world around them (participation restrictions).”

People with disabilities have an increased risk for developing chronic health conditions, such as diabetes or heart disease. They also often spend more on healthcare costs and consequently may experience more financial hardship than those without a disability.

For more information about the Community Health Profiles Data Initiative, please see the initiative homepage.

results.name: Living_Near_Recreational_Space
results.title: Population within 10-Minute Walk of a Recreational Space
results.description:
This indicator provides information about the percentage of the total population that is within a 10-minute walk of a publicly available recreational space.

In well-designed communities, homes, stores, schools, and recreational spaces are connected by safe walking routes, providing an opportunity for all community members to enjoy the outdoors and experience physical and mental health benefits. The closer a person lives to a park, the more likely they are to walk or bike to that park and to use it for exercise. Living within a half mile of a park is associated with higher levels of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity among community members.

For more information about the Community Health Profiles Data Initiative, please see the initiative homepage.

results.description:
Vnitřní členění Protektorátu Čechy a Morava v letech 1942-1945

Hranice vnitřního členění Protektorátu Čechy a Morava v letech 1942-1945 byly vytvořeny na podkladu map III. vojenského mapování v měřítku 1 : 75  000 a 1 : 200  000 a agregací vektorové vrstvy sčítacích volebních okrsků z roku 2021. Všechny dostupné podkladové mapy byly zgeoreferencovány a následně využity při vektorizaci hranic Protektorátu. Datový soubor je rozdělen do 4 vrstev obsahující informace o vnitřním členění na úrovni politických okresů, krajů, zemí a celého protektorátu.

results.name: biosds1753_fpu
results.title: Northern Rubber Boa Range - CWHR R046a [ds1753]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. Each focal taxon’s location data was extracted (when applicable) from the following list of sources. BIOS datasets are bracketed with their “ds” numbers and can be located on CDFW’s BIOS viewer: https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS.

  • California Natural Diversity Database,

  • Terrestrial Species Monitoring [ds2826],

  • North American Bat Monitoring Data Portal,

  • VertNet,

  • Breeding Bird Survey,

  • Wildlife Insights,

  • eBird,

  • iNaturalist,

  • other available CDFW or partner data.
tags: California Department of Fish And Wildlife
results.snippet:
The species range dataset represents the generalized geographic area within which the species is expected to regularly occur within California, without consideration of specific habitat requirements. Generally, range map boundaries are based on mapped species occurrence locations and expert knowledge and aligned with ecologically relevant units such as ecoregions or watersheds. The California Wildlife Habitat Relationship (CWHR) ranges have been developed over three decades and vary in age of last update. The date of last update can be found in the CWHR Revision Tracking Table at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=115517. 

GIS vector datasets representing species ranges are one component of the CWHR system. This system includes a web application that supplies information on California’s terrestrial vertebrates and the habitats upon which they depend, supports user queries, and houses spatial data on habitats and wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species that occur in California. CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of regularly occurring terrestrial vertebrate species within California. These range datasets are used to generate a tabular database of species locations by county, ecoregion, and several other jurisdictional delineations to inform the CWHR system. This enables users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. The species range datasets are also used by many groups to assist with development of biological surveys, and within CDFW to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning. 

For more information about the CWHR system, visit the CWHR Homepage: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

Appropriate uses of CWHR data include planning for site-specific biological surveys or anticipating general trends in habitat suitability for particular species resulting from management actions which may reshape habitat composition and structure (see comparison queries in the CWHR application). Neither the CWHR GIS data representing a species’ range, nor the data representing predicted suitable habitat replace the need for field surveys to confirm the presence or potential absence of a particular species at any specific site. Similarly, GIS data concerning the distribution of habitats does not replace the need for field surveys to verify the composition of habitat or vegetation communities at any specific site.

14-tuoju tikslu siekiama išsaugoti vandenynus, jūras ir jūrų išteklius ir užtikrinti tausų jų naudojimą. Tai apima jūrų ir pakrančių ekosistemų apsaugą, išsaugant bent 10 proc. pakrančių ir jūrų teritorijų, taip pat jūrų taršos ir vandenynų rūgštėjimo padarinių prevenciją ir mažinimą. Siekiant pagerinti jūrų ir vandenynų sveikatą, svarbu gilinti mokslo žinias, mokslinių tyrimų pajėgumus ir jūrų technologijas.

results.title: Western Yellow-billed Cuckoo Range - CWHR B259a [ds3262]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. Each focal taxon’s location data was extracted (when applicable) from the following list of sources. BIOS datasets are bracketed with their “ds” numbers and can be located on CDFW’s BIOS viewer: https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS.

  • California Natural Diversity Database,

  • Terrestrial Species Monitoring [ds2826],

  • North American Bat Monitoring Data Portal,

  • VertNet,

  • Breeding Bird Survey,

  • Wildlife Insights,

  • eBird,

  • iNaturalist,

  • other available CDFW or partner data.
tags: California Department of Fish And Wildlife
results.snippet:
The species range dataset represents the generalized geographic area within which the species is expected to regularly occur within California, without consideration of specific habitat requirements. Generally, range map boundaries are based on mapped species occurrence locations and expert knowledge and aligned with ecologically relevant units such as ecoregions or watersheds. The California Wildlife Habitat Relationship (CWHR) ranges have been developed over three decades and vary in age of last update. The date of last update can be found in the CWHR Revision Tracking Table at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=115517. 

GIS vector datasets representing species ranges are one component of the CWHR system. This system includes a web application that supplies information on California’s terrestrial vertebrates and the habitats upon which they depend, supports user queries, and houses spatial data on habitats and wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species that occur in California. CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of regularly occurring terrestrial vertebrate species within California. These range datasets are used to generate a tabular database of species locations by county, ecoregion, and several other jurisdictional delineations to inform the CWHR system. This enables users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. The species range datasets are also used by many groups to assist with development of biological surveys, and within CDFW to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning. 

For more information about the CWHR system, visit the CWHR Homepage: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

This CWHR dataset should not be used to extend any analytical inference beyond that warranted by the nature of the data as it has been described in all sections of this metadata. Appropriate uses of CWHR data include planning for site-specific biological surveys or anticipating general trends in habitat suitability for particular species resulting from management actions which may reshape habitat composition and structure (see comparison queries in the CWHR application). Neither the CWHR GIS data representing a species’ range, nor the data representing predicted suitable habitat replace the need for field surveys to confirm the presence or potential absence of a particular species at any specific site. Similarly, GIS data concerning the distribution of habitats does not replace the need for field surveys to verify the composition of habitat or vegetation communities at any specific site.

results.description:
LT
12 TIKSLAS. Užtikrinti darnius vartojimo ir gamybos modelius:
12-tuoju tikslu siekiama užtikrinti darnius vartojimo ir gamybos modelius, kuriant atitinkamą aplinkos apsaugos politiką. Siekdamos šio tikslo šalys kuria nacionalinius veiksmų planus, pasirašo tarptautinius daugiašalius aplinkosaugos susitarimus ir skiria paramą besivystančių šalių mokslo ir technologiniams gebėjimams stiprinti – tai prioritetinė nacionalinės politikos sritis. Į darnaus vartojimo ir gamybos modelių užtikrinimą skatinama įtraukti ne tik bendroves, bet ir visą visuomenę, informacijai skleisti pasitelkiant visų lygių švietimą.
12.c. Uždavinys: Racionalizuoti neveiksmingas iškastinio kuro subsidijas, skatinančias eikvojantį vartojimą, pašalinant rinkos iškraipymus remiantis nacionalinėmis aplinkybėmis, įskaitant mokesčių pertvarkymą ir laipsnišką šių žalingų subsidijų nutraukimą ten, kur jos teikiamos, siekiant atspindėti jų poveikį aplinkai, visapusiškai atsižvelgiant į ypatingus besivystančių šalių poreikius ir sąlygas, taip pat kuo labiau sumažinti galimą neigiamą poveikį jų vystymuisi neturtingas ir paveiktas bendruomenes apsaugančiu būdu.
12.c.1. JT rodiklis: Iškastinio kuro subsidijų (gamybos ir vartojimo) suma vienam BVP vienetui.

Goal 12. Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns:
Goal 12 is aimed at ensuring sustainable consumption and production patterns through development of appropriate environmental policies. To achieve this goal, countries develop national action plans, sign international multilateral environmental agreements and provide support for strengthening the scientific and technological capacity of developing countries – this is priority of national policy. Ensuring sustainable consumption and production patterns encourages involvement not only of companies but of the society by disseminating information through all levels of education.
12.c. Goal: Rationalize inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies that encourage wasteful consumption by removing market distortions, in accordance with national circumstances, including by restructuring taxation and phasing out those harmful subsidies, where they exist, to reflect their environmental impacts, taking fully into account the specific needs and conditions of developing countries and minimizing the possible adverse impacts on their development in a manner that protects the poor and the affected communities.
12.c.1. UN indicator: Amount of fossil-fuel subsidies per unit of GDP (production and consumption).
     Units: billions of nominal United States dollars
Source: UN Global SDG Indicators Database

results.title: Santa Catalina Island Fox Range - CWHR M150a [ds3288]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

The following data sources were collated for the purposes of range mapping and species habitat modeling by RADMAP. Each focal taxon’s location data was extracted (when applicable) from the following list of sources. BIOS datasets are bracketed with their “ds” numbers and can be located on CDFW’s BIOS viewer: https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS.

  • California Natural Diversity Database,

  • Terrestrial Species Monitoring [ds2826],

  • North American Bat Monitoring Data Portal,

  • VertNet,

  • Breeding Bird Survey,

  • Wildlife Insights,

  • eBird,

  • iNaturalist,

  • other available CDFW or partner data.
tags: California Department of Fish And Wildlife
results.snippet:
The species range dataset represents the generalized geographic area within which the species is expected to regularly occur within California, without consideration of specific habitat requirements. Generally, range map boundaries are based on mapped species occurrence locations and expert knowledge and aligned with ecologically relevant units such as ecoregions or watersheds. The California Wildlife Habitat Relationship (CWHR) ranges have been developed over three decades and vary in age of last update. The date of last update can be found in the CWHR Revision Tracking Table at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=115517. 

GIS vector datasets representing species ranges are one component of the CWHR system. This system includes a web application that supplies information on California’s terrestrial vertebrates and the habitats upon which they depend, supports user queries, and houses spatial data on habitats and wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species that occur in California. CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of regularly occurring terrestrial vertebrate species within California. These range datasets are used to generate a tabular database of species locations by county, ecoregion, and several other jurisdictional delineations to inform the CWHR system. This enables users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. The species range datasets are also used by many groups to assist with development of biological surveys, and within CDFW to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning. 

For more information about the CWHR system, visit the CWHR Homepage: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.

results.title: FIRM Zone A Approximate Base Flood Elevations
results.description:
Approximate Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) within FEMA's Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) "A" zones, effective August 28, 2008. BFEs were determined by PBS&J June 2009. Attribute FLDZON_NUM added on 20090617 to assign a numeric value to FIRM zone; higher number, higher risk.

This dataset was developed by PBS&J under contract with Lee County Department of Natural Resources to estimate base flood elevations (BFEs) within FEMA's Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) "A" zones (effective August 28, 2008). The BFEs derived in this process are approximate estimates of base flood elevation within "A" flood zones where BFEs are undetermined by FEMA. Applicants needing an accurate BFE determination should submit current topographic information of the site to the Building Department.

The PBSJcomment field explains how the BFEs were determined. Some of the common ones are: Approximated based on average elevation…/estimated from ground tin: these were estimated with the new (2007) LiDAR data, either through the creation of a TIN or from the GRIDs provided. Typically station points were computed along the boundaries, and the elevations at these points were used to approximate what the elevation was Follows Contours/FromContour: These were approximated from the old (1998) contour data. A lot of the boundaries are right on top of the contour, so in these cases we just gave it the value of the contour From HEC-RAS…: Many times, at the upstream end of the riverine studies, they added an approximate floodplain at the elevation of the most upstream cross section from the detailed model

results.title: California Brown Pelican Range - CWHR B043a [ds3282]
results.description: Vector datasets of CWHR range maps are one component of California Wildlife Habitat Relationships (CWHR), a comprehensive information system and predictive model for California's wildlife. The CWHR System was developed to support habitat conservation and management, land use planning, impact assessment, education, and research involving terrestrial vertebrates in California. CWHR contains information on life history, management status, geographic distribution, and habitat relationships for wildlife species known to occur regularly in California. Range maps represent the maximum, current geographic extent of each species within California. They were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. For more information about CWHR, visit the CWHR webpage (https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR). The webpage provides links to download CWHR data and user documents such as a look up table of available range maps including species code, species name, and range map revision history; a full set of CWHR GIS data; .pdf files of each range map or species life history accounts; and a User Guide.
tags: California Department of Fish And Wildlife
results.snippet: Range maps of California's regularly-occurring vertebrates were digitized as GIS layers to support the predictions of the CWHR System software, which allows users to query for wildlife species meeting a set of location and habitat conditions. Presently, they are used to help generate a tabular location database for the system software. Outside the system software, the GIS layers are used to support species richness assessments for statewide conservation planning.

results.name: biosds3295_fpu
results.title: Light-footed Ridgway's Rail Range - CWHR B144a [ds3295]
results.description:
CWHR species range datasets represent the maximum current geographic extent of each species within California. Ranges were originally delineated at a scale of 1:5,000,000 by species-level experts more than 30 years ago and have gradually been revised at a scale of 1:1,000,000. Species occurrence data are used in defining species ranges, but range polygons may extend beyond the limits of extant occurrence data for a particular species. When drawing range boundaries, CDFW seeks to err on the side of commission rather than omission. This means that CDFW may include areas within a range based on expert knowledge or other available information, despite an absence of confirmed occurrences, which may be due to a lack of survey effort. The degree to which a range polygon is extended beyond occurrence data will vary among species, depending upon each species’ vagility, dispersal patterns, and other ecological and life history factors. The boundary line of a range polygon is drawn with consideration of these factors and is aligned with standardized boundaries including watersheds (NHD), ecoregions (USDA), or other ecologically meaningful delineations such as elevation contour lines. While CWHR ranges are meant to represent the current range, once an area has been designated as part of a species’ range in CWHR, it will remain part of the range even if there have been no documented occurrences within recent decades. An area is not removed from the range polygon unless experts indicate that it has not been occupied for a number of years after repeated surveys or is deemed no longer suitable and unlikely to be recolonized. It is important to note that range polygons typically contain areas in which a species is not expected to be found due to the patchy configuration of suitable habitat within a species’ range. In this regard, range polygons are coarse generalizations of where a species may be found. This data is available for download from the CDFW website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CWHR.
